note: Per-asset waivers, each one a measured value and a reason. An entry here does NOT switch a check off: the check still runs, still measures, and `assets:validate` prints the asset as `warn` rather than `ok`. `assets:report` counts them and the count is part of the asset state in PROJECT_MEMORY. Adding an entry is a deliberate act with a date against it; a new asset that fails the same check is still a failure until somebody writes it down here. Raised by ADR-013.

exceptions.measured: upper-left mean 158.2 vs lower-right 165.5 (delta -7.3) — the key light is not coming from the upper left (ASSET_PIPELINE §1.1 LIGHT: single key from the north-west, 35 degrees)
exceptions.reason: Delivered art, accepted under ADR-013. The check splits the alpha bounding box on its anti-diagonal, which biases against light-bodied and diagonally-massed silhouettes: the same rig part passes facing se/nw and fails facing ne/sw, and every vehicle that fails is a near-white body whose windscreen and headlights fall in the lower-right half of the box. A visual review of the worst eight found no relit asset in the set — the key light is consistent, the instrument is not.

exceptions.measured: 171px exceeds the 125px projected box +15% = 144px (ASSET_PIPELINE §1.2 (50 px ≈ 0.78 m))
exceptions.reason: Delivered art, accepted under ADR-013. The set is drawn at a shallower camera than the world's 2:1 dimetric, so a subject's silhouette is taller relative to its width than the projection predicts. `assets:import` fits sprites to the projected WIDTH because the footprint is what parks, queues and sorts; the height then overflows by the amount the camera differs. Measured overflow here is under 40%, which reads as an object standing slightly proud of its own ground diamond rather than as a wrong object.
